key_idea: The cost of an interval depends only on the fingers on the two consecutive notes, so a DP over (note index, finger used) with 5 states suffices.
sketch: Parse the four tables into T[colour pair][lower finger][upper finger][half steps], marking finger pairs that are not listed as unavailable. dp[i][f] = min difficulty of the first i notes ending on finger f; for a transition determine the lower/upper key, colour pair (key mod 12 in {2,5,7,10,0} is black) and distance, and map the previous/next finger to (lower, upper) depending on direction. A repeated note forces the same finger at cost 0. Answer is the min over the last finger; O(25 L). Pitfalls: descending intervals swap the finger roles, only listed finger pairs may be used, and 0 entries are treated as legal zero cost (in the sample they only occur at impossible colour/distance combinations).
